findings.highlight: No matter how many people you bring, none will return alive.
findings.evidenceJa: —今日だけは、何人たりとも生きては帰れん。
findings.governingReading: Today, no person whatsoever will return alive; imagined trees voice an absolute warning.
findings.explanation: Whoever enters is recast as any number of people Shirou brings.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka's the first to break the ice.
findings.evidenceJa: ……先に構えを解いたのは遠坂だった。
findings.governingReading: Rin asks Shirou to lower the sword and is the first to release her stance; he then lowers his wooden sword. The omitted detail is her physical de-escalation, not all of her initiative.
findings.explanation: Rin still ends the deadlock first, but break the ice omits her release of her fighting stance. Both versions keep Shirou lowering his wooden sword after her request.

findings.highlight: "That too. But Tohsaka, you won't get out unscathed if you fight her. You're bound to get hurt once you start. I don't want that to happen. To begin with—"
findings.evidenceJa: 「それもあるけど。遠坂、イリヤと戦ったらただじゃ済まないぞ。始めたらどっちかが必ず傷を負う。そういうのは嫌だ。俺は、もともと」
findings.governingReading: Shirou objects because either Rin or Illya will be injured if they fight.
findings.explanation: Shirou's objection to either girl being injured becomes a warning that Rin will be hurt. His explicit concern for Illya within this appeal disappears.

findings.highlight: Still, Tohsaka's doing me a favor by letting me guide her.
findings.evidenceJa: けどまあ、案内をする分には、遠坂は俺を優先してくれる。
findings.governingReading: As long as he serves as guide, Rin will give his plan priority; taking her keeps her from challenging Illya independently.
findings.explanation: Rin prioritizing Shirou while he guides becomes her doing him a favor.
